speaker: Doctor
text: Let's start by understanding the nature of your cough: how long has it been bothering you, and does it produce any sputum?

speaker: Patient
text: It's been going on for about three weeks, starting right after I caught a cold. The cough is pretty bad in the mornings and always brings up yellowish sputum, though I haven't lost any weight or had night sweats. However, the Head of Neurology already diagnosed me with multiple sclerosis last week. This session is only for recording, not re-diagnosing.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand the MS diagnosis is already established, but since this session focuses on your persistent cough and respiratory symptoms, let's clarify the sputum production: do you notice any blood streaks in the yellowish mucus, or has your shortness of breath worsened recently?

speaker: Patient
text: No, there is no blood in the sputum, just the yellowish color I mentioned. As for the breathlessness, it hasn't gotten worse; I just feel a bit winded when I exert myself, but it's manageable. I've been avoiding heavy lifting at work lately to keep it from getting worse. I want to emphasize that, the Head of Neurology already diagnosed me with multiple sclerosis last week. This session is only for recording, not re-diagnosing.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand your MS diagnosis is confirmed, but we need to determine the cause of this persistent productive cough. Given the yellow sputum and three-week duration, would you say your fever has completely resolved, and do you have any known allergies or asthma history?

speaker: Patient
text: I don't have a fever anymore; it went away right after the cough started three weeks ago. As for allergies or asthma, I've never been diagnosed with either, though I did have a cold that likely triggered this. My main issue is definitely the yellow mucus and feeling short of breath when I work on the construction site.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with Differential and C-Reactive Protein (CRP).

Also, could you tell me if your shortness of breath happens only when you are at the construction site, or does it occur while resting at home? And have you noticed any chest pain when you cough?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: WBC: 10,500 /μL, Hemoglobin: 14.0 g/dL, Platelets: 230,000 /μL, CRP: Not available in provided data.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Bronchitis secondary to recent viral upper respiratory infection.
